Topic: How sure am I, really?
Story (story.md): Opening — coffee studies, ninety-five-percent-accurate tests, seventy-percent-chance-of-rain, juries. Each phrase hides a threshold nobody ever pulls apart.
Technical (chapter.md): Carried from Ch 1: we saw 6/10 heads. Frequentist said p=0.75; Bayesian said P(p>0.5) about 0.73. Two answers, same data. Now make them precise.

Topic: Eggplants, press releases, and the number at the bottom
Story (story.md): Teenager-and-mom anecdote: 'studies show eggplant causes cancer'. The chain ends at a number that passed some threshold.
Technical (chapter.md): Framing: most of statistics is staring at that number.

Topic: Back to the coin — where is the line?
Story (story.md): At 3 heads, at 5/10, at fractions near half over thousands — how sure am I at each stage? When does 'consistent with fair' become 'convinces me it is fair'?
Technical (chapter.md): We never know for sure. Both lenses live with that and turn it into something we can act on.

Topic: Imagine 10,000 people each tossing a fair coin 100 times
Story (story.md): The 10,000 imagined crowd: 796 got 50, 780 got 49 or 51, nine got 35, practically none got 25. Image story/ten_thousand_people.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Try/Observe: pretend the coin is fair; toss 100 times; ask which counts are common.

Topic: Fair coins can still produce 35 heads
Story (story.md): About 9 of 10,000 did. Rarely does not mean never. The picture is about how often, not which results are impossible.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Observe: counts at/below 39 or at/above 61 happen about 3.5% of the time combined. That's below the 5% budget because no integer cutoff hits 5% exactly.

Topic: Drawing the surprise line — 80%, 90%, 95%
Story (story.md): Casino friend confirms 95% as the everyday default; physicist friend wants five-sigma. The 95% convention is a convention, not a law.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Frequentist take: the green tail region is the rejection region. Threshold is alpha; turn it up or down as a knob.

Topic: The 5% surprise tails, cutoffs at 39 and 61
Story (story.md): Symmetric two-tailed cutoffs: 39 and below, or 61 and above land in the blue surprise zone. Image story/surprise_tails.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Frequentist: two-sided alpha=0.05 test at N=100 rejects at k<=39 or k>=61.

Topic: Observations on the chart: 50, 55, 60, 65, 70
Story (story.md): Arrows at each observation; 50 and 55 sit in red unsurprising; 65 and 70 are in blue; 60 is just inside the red edge. Image story/my_observations_on_the_chart.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Same chart underlies the frequentist rejection rule.

Topic: Alpha is an upper bound, not a probability the coin is rigged
Story (story.md): SKIP: technical clarification, no story version
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Bayesian take: with Beta(1,1) prior and 50/100, posterior Beta(51,51), CI about [0.40, 0.60]; at 60/100, Beta(61,41), P(p>0.5) about 0.97. Alpha is an upper bound on false-positive rate, not Prob(rigged | data).

Topic: How to actually build a biased coin
Story (story.md): Detour: Diaconis says adding mass to a flipped coin barely works; bend the coin into a cup; spin on edge; replace a face. Threshold-shifting in the simulator vs metalwork at home.
Technical (chapter.md): Not covered (story-only physics aside).

Topic: Biased coin overlaid with fair coin at p=0.55
Story (story.md): Blue fair crowd, red 0.55-biased crowd, side by side at N=100. The two humps overlap heavily around 53. Image story/fair_vs_biased_overlap.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Implicit in Loop D — small bias hides inside the fair-coin surprise zone.

Topic: Red zone means 'data not strong enough', not 'coin is fair'
Story (story.md): The rule has an asymmetry: it lets us conclude bias when we see the blue zone, but it never lets us conclude 'fair' from the red zone.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Compare: the frequentist test only ever fails to reject H0; it never accepts it. 'Failed to reject' is not 'believes fair'.

Topic: Both lenses at every possible observation
Story (story.md): SKIP: technical-only comparison
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Try/Observe: for every k from 0 to N, plot frequentist p-value and Bayesian P(p>0.5). At N=10 the two lines cross their thresholds at different k; at N=100 they roughly line up (two-sided freq paired with one-sided posterior — coincidence of the symmetric prior). Image decision_curves.png.

Topic: Prior sensitivity: flat vs skeptical vs heads-low
Story (story.md): Three starting lines meet the same data. Fair-leaning prior barely moves at 60/100; heads-low prior drags up but stays under 0.5; with 600/1000 every prior lands near the same place. Small samples = prior is loud, large samples = data is. Image story/prior_sensitivity.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Probe: Beta(50,50) with 6/10 barely moves; with 60/100 moves noticeably; with 600/1000 matches the frequentist. Beta(2,8) at 6/10 gives posterior Beta(8,12), mean 0.4, P(p>0.5) about 0.18.

Topic: Alpha is a knob with consequences in both directions
Story (story.md): Three panels of the same chart at 10%, 5%, 1% in the tails. Image story/threshold_knob.png. Wider zone = more alarms (some false); narrower zone = fewer alarms but misses real biases.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop C Try/Observe: sampling distribution at alpha=0.10/0.05/0.01 rejects outside [42,58] / [40,60] / [37,63]. Image alpha_sweep.png.

Topic: Why not push alpha to zero?
Story (story.md): Zero tails means empty surprise zone, the rule never fires, so the detection rate is also zero. The threshold is the price to pay for firing at all.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop C Question: no abstract 'right' alpha. The Bayesian counterpart is the credible-interval level and the action threshold on posterior probability.

Topic: Threshold should match stakes
Story (story.md): Beer-round = 10% is fine. Drug-approval = 1% may still be too loose; cost of a missed effect is depriving sick people. Honest reading of p<0.05: a budget for being fooled by chance.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop C Bayesian counterpart: same trade-off, different control surface (ship if P(beneficial) > 0.95).

Topic: The hump narrows as N grows
Story (story.md): Four overlaid curves at N=50, 100, 500, 5000 on the fraction axis, all centered at 0.5, spread shrinks with N. Image story/hump_narrows_with_n.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Motivates Loop D — bigger N shrinks the unsurprising zone in fraction terms, so small biases can no longer hide.

Topic: Ask the inverse question — belief curve
Story (story.md): Blank-slate starting point: any bias from 0 to 1 equally plausible. After 60/100, belief curve centered just above 0.6; 95% band runs from about 0.502 to 0.69, with 0.5 just outside the lower edge. Image story/belief_after_60.png.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop A Bayesian: Beta(1,1) + 60/100 = Beta(61,41), center 0.598, P(p>0.5) about 0.97. Same math, flipped question.

Topic: Two answers for 60/100 — procedure vs state of mind
Story (story.md): Way one: 60 lands in the unsurprising zone, rule does not fire. Way two: belief moves, lean toward biased but only by a hair. Courtroom analogy: burden of proof vs juror's quiet hunch.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Hunch: both lenses can say 'I am 95% sure' but 'sure of what?' differs. Frequentist conditions on H0; Bayesian assigns posterior probability to p given prior and model.

Topic: Each lens fails differently
Story (story.md): SKIP: technical-only contrast
Technical (chapter.md): Frequentist fails when we want to believe something rather than merely fail to reject. Bayesian fails when a public decision cannot depend on whose prior. Bayes factor deferred to Ch 6.

Topic: How often does the rule fool me?
Story (story.md): 1000 fake experiments at truths p=0.50/0.52/0.55/0.60 across N=50/200/1000. Image story/how_often_I_get_fooled.png. Fair coin: about 5% alarms at every N (the budget). Slightly biased (0.52) at N=1000: about 20% catch rate.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop D Try/Observe: 2000 experiments per cell. Under p=0.50, 3-5% rejections (discrete test is conservative). At p=0.52: 4%/7%/23%. At p=0.55: 8%/26%/88%. At p=0.60: 23%/79%/~100%. Image rejection_rates.png.

Topic: Three knobs at once: bias size, N, threshold
Story (story.md): Small bias hidden in small experiment looks like a fair coin. Most of real life lives in the middle of the chart.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop D Hunch: 'how often will I be fooled' depends on alpha, N, and the truth. Alpha controls false positives; N+truth control true positives.

Topic: Same machinery, different clothes
Story (story.md): Drug trials
Technical (chapter.md): juries at beyond-reasonable-doubt
Play: 95%-accurate tests with 1-in-1000 prevalence giving mostly false positives. Same shape in serious clothes.

Topic: Hand-off: how big a sample do I need?
Story (story.md): For a 1pp lift, how many tosses? Rule has a threshold for false alarms but not for catching real things. Where does that come from?
Technical (chapter.md): Big question opening Ch 3: power. Given an effect worth catching, how do we plan N so the test actually catches it?
